drafted_from: tool:add-captions's own row in tools/media-composition/tool-rows.json, tools/media-composition/do-work/cut-and-caption.mjs (the script this tool runs), tools/media-composition/read-data/caption-styles.json, and the script run on a synthetic 7 second clip
start_here: Say to your AI: "Burn captions into my video from its transcript, with the words lighting up as they are said." It runs tool:add-captions and saves the captioned video in your files.
no_lists_because: It makes a new video in your files from the video you name and keeps no list of its own.
instructions: 1. Get the timed words of the video: run the speech-to-text tool on the video's sound (tool:extract-sound makes a small audio file for it) or write a list of {text, start, end} words.

2. Say "Add captions to this video" with the clip (name source.mp4, its identity and exact byte length from your files), the transcript, and a style: subtitles, emphasis, spoken-words, serif-spoken-words or white-words-light-up (default subtitles). Use transcript_from if the transcript's zero is not the video's start.

3. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run and tool tool:add-captions. The door runs it in a container and answers {"result": {...}}; an error comes back as {"error": "what to change"}.
4. Read result.captions (how many caption lines were burned in) and files.video, the captioned video in your files.

worked_examples.title: Two caption lines, words light up as said
worked_examples.ask: Caption my video with white words that light up.
worked_examples.given: read from tools/media-composition/do-work/cut-and-caption.mjs and run on a 7 second clip: the seven words fall in two gaps of speech (0.2 to 1.6 s and 4.2 to 5.6 s), so they gather into two lines
